reader.title: Killing of Ovide Belizaire
bases: A band of masked, armed men forced their way into Belizaire's cabin at night and shot him dead in front of his family; no lawful authority is mentioned (A1).

A1 reports Belizaire killed by 'a number of armed men' acting with no lawful authority, but the only motive given is that the party was hunting another Black man, Soulouque, who had 'given offense'; no accusation against Belizaire himself was reported, so the pretext is unclear.
The only report found is one editorial, written by the Lafayette Gazette and reprinted in the Abbeville Meridional (A1); the Gazette's local-column account it refers to was not found.

summary.text: The killing of Ovide Belizaire was the fatal shooting of a Black man in his own house in Louisiana, by a band of masked, armed men, at night shortly before 3 August 1895.
A coroner's inquest placed the guilt on no one, and the Lafayette Gazette, in an editorial reprinted by the Abbeville Meridional, condemned the killing as an unprovoked murder.
According to testimony at the coroner's inquest, the armed party had been searching for another Black man, Soulouque, who "seems to have given offense to some people in that section".
The coverage does not say what that offense was, or name the place beyond "that section".
Belizaire was at home with his wife and children when "a number of armed men" forced their way into his cabin and shot him.
His family was too frightened to recognize any of them.
Wounded by a bullet in the head and another in the lungs, Belizaire jumped out through a window and walked a few feet from the house.
He was found dead there the next morning, with his shotgun nearby.
Coroner Gladu held an inquest, and the evidence, while placing the guilt on no one, showed in the Gazette's view that a premeditated murder had been committed.
No report of arrests, a grand jury or a trial was found in the coverage.
The only surviving account is an editorial headed "A Revolting Murder", written by the Lafayette Gazette and reprinted in the Abbeville Meridional on 3 August 1895.
The editorial refers to a fuller account in the Gazette's local column, which was not found.
The Gazette took the victim's side, calling the attackers "a gang of desporate [desperate] hoodlums" and saying Belizaire was shot "in his own house where he had a perfect right to be".
It added that he had probably been killed for trying to defend himself, and asked what crime he had been guilty of to be "shown so little mercy".
No report of the killing was found in the Black press.

accounts.label: Lafayette Gazette editorial (summarizing coroner's inquest evidence)
accounts.gist: Armed men forced their way into the cabin of a peaceable Black man and killed him before his family while hunting another man, Soulouque; the editor knew of no excuse and suggested Belizaire was probably killed for trying to defend himself.

framing.detail: Headed 'A Revolting Murder'; the Gazette called the killing 'cowardly, premeditated and unprooked [unprovoked]' and 'a most barbarous and revolting crime', and the Meridional reprinted it as editorial matter.

record_check.dossier: Ovide Belizaire ('Divide' is an OCR misreading of the Meridional page)
Before 1895-08-03 (date of the reprint); the killing itself is undated and may fall in late July
Not stated; the story came from the Lafayette Gazette's local column, and the locality is given only as 'that section'
None against Belizaire; the band was reportedly hunting Soulouque, who had 'given offense'
Probable lynching: killed illegally by a band of armed men; pretext unclear
Add that the inquest placed the guilt on no one, and that the account is a Lafayette Gazette editorial reprinted in the Abbeville Meridional

info: Before 3 August 1895, at night ('midnight tragedy'); exact date not stated
Belizaire's own house ('humble cabin'); the locality is given only as 'that section'
None against Belizaire; the editor wrote that no excuse for the killing had been advanced and no crime of his was known
A band of masked, armed men, unidentified; the wife and children were too frightened to recognize any of them

sources.note: "A Revolting Murder": editorial credited to the Lafayette Gazette; names Ovide Belizaire, killed at home by a band of masked, armed men; coroner's inquest fixed guilt on no one; men were searching for Soulouque.
quotes: a number of armed men forced their way into his humble cabin and killed him under the very eyes of his wife and children, who unfortunately were too frightened to recognize any of them
the party of men were searching for the negro Soulouque who seems to have given offense to some people in that section
What this poor negro had done to deserve such punishment no one seems to know.
